sentences: On a moonlit, arid desert a woman in a striped robe lies deeply asleep, still holding her staff, while a maned lion approaches and cautiously sniffs at her.
Beside her lie a mandolin and a tall, slender-necked water jar.
Henri Rousseau described the scene himself: a wandering mandolin player overcome by fatigue, and a lion that picks up her scent yet does not devour her.
Rousseau had no formal art training and painted with simple shapes and broad blocks of colour, which is exactly what gives the scene its still, dreamlike strangeness.
He first showed the picture at the Salon des Indépendants in 1897 and tried, without success, to sell it to the mayor of his hometown, Laval.
It then sat in the collection of a Paris charcoal merchant until it resurfaced in 1924, and in 1939 it was given to the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
Today it hangs in the same gallery as Van Gogh's The Starry Night.
